It added a new wrapper channel method, switch. Its refusals are human-typing, turn-running, dialog-pending, unverified-cli, no-session, child-not-ended and resume-failed. The served channel methods go from 9 to 10 requests plus the one notification.
The outer-PTY pump can now respawn its child under the same host terminal. It opens a new pseudo-terminal pair sized to the host. The human's keystroke copy persists across the respawn, and viola writes no byte to the terminal.
It added a new compiled time bound, RESPAWN_REAP_BOUND, at 10 s. A child that has not exited inside it is not replaced, and the switch is refused not-delivered child-not-ended.
viola --help's setup: row now reads open, run, revive, adopt, up, switch, verify, plugin install (17 to 18 served verbs). send gains four hint causes, and a send is refused turn-running while a switch stands.
Everything was proven over the fake agent only and no capability is claimed. Forks F1, F3, F5 and F6 stand PROVISIONAL on the delegate overseer's word. The real-CLI readings R6a and R6b are carried, not fired.

body:
Added a new CLI verb, viola switch <name> with --model and/or --effort and --json, which moves a running wrapped session to a given model and effort. The user's own settings are not written.
Added a new wrapper channel method, switch, taking sender, model and effort. It reads no from. It answers ok with the pair, or refuses with human-typing, turn-running, dialog-pending, unverified-cli, no-session, child-not-ended or resume-failed. A missing, wrongly typed or failing half is -32602 with data null.
The PTY pump can now respawn its child in place: it reaps the old child within a new 10 s RESPAWN_REAP_BOUND (PROVISIONAL, F6), then spawns claude --resume <id> on the new pair in a new pseudo-terminal under the same host terminal. A switch appends one launch line, plus the window line again where the snapshot holds one, and rewrites the snapshot's launch and child_pid.
The channel's closed method-label list grows from 10 to 11 with switch. While a switch stands, sends are refused turn-running. After the respawn, the old child's late session-end of the switched id is screened once.
Everything is proven over the fake agent alone and no capability is claimed. F1, F3, F5 and F6 stand PROVISIONAL on the delegate overseer's word. The real-CLI readings R6a and R6b are carried to the fleet on the founder's host.

body: The CLI process-log file rows, one per verb: viola switch is a new verb that logs as cli into cli-<name>.ndjson. No row holds it yet.
The manual dispatch span per cli verb: cli.switch is a new span name.
The process-exit detail rows for exit 1 by verb: switch adds no exit-1 detail of its own. Its exit 1 is the cli catch site's internal-error alone. A row expecting an exit-1-switch row is not carried.
The rows on channel-request and channel-response lines and their closed method label: the label list grows from 10 to 11 (switch), so the switch pair names its method.
The rows on channel invalid-params causes (-32602): the switch method answers -32602 with data null on neither half, a half of another type, or a half failing its check.
The rows on channel params sender and the unauthenticated from: the switch method takes sender and reads no from.

The rows on RefusalReason detail words and driver-side refusals ending a channel-response with result_class refusal and no word: switch keeps that shape. The four new words dialog-pending, no-session, child-not-ended and resume-failed appear in no diag line.
The diag-line schema and the rule that removes schema words no build can emit: the schema is unchanged and none of the four new words was entered, because no line emits one.
The wrapper send-refused turn-running detail: a send is now also refused turn-running from a switch's request until the new child's session-start.

The run process log's claude-child process-start and process-exit lines: a switch ends the old child (exit through kill-fallback on the respawn's SIGHUP) and starts a new one, adding a claude-child pair per switch.
The PTY seam log events (spawn, kill-fallback) and the pty.spawn span attribute row: the respawn runs under the existing pty.spawn span and reaps the old child through the kill fallback.
The decision that the panic arm kills the child: the pump's panic arm now kills the current, possibly respawned, child.

The launch-line-untraced and window-line-untraced decisions and the run start events order: a switch appends one launch line after the reap and before the respawn, then the recorded window line again. These are events-log appends outside a start.

The rows on product readers reading the snapshot through replay: a switch rewrites the snapshot's launch and child_pid, and the switch reads pending_dialog, agent_session_id, launch and window through replay.
The hook-invoked and hook-decision rows for session-end: after a respawn, the old child's late session-end of the switched id is screened once. No row says what a hook line after a respawn means.

The NEVER-log floor rows (no params or results in channel lines, session id never logged, child settings argument never logged): the switch logs no pair, model or session id, and passes no --settings.
The unreadable or unverified ledger rows and the unverified-cli refusal: the switch refuses unverified-cli from the start's cli_verified.
The CLI stderr unable / hint pair rows: four new hint causes, with no hint naming viola release.
The child exit from the process handle decisions: the pump now waits on and reaps a child it replaces, within a 10 s bound, and refuses child-not-ended past it.

body_fields.fact: viola switch logs as cli into cli-<name>.ndjson under the manual dispatch span cli.switch, with process-start and process-exit. A refusal ends process-exit with no detail, as send's does.
The wrapper's switch channel method (PROVISIONAL, F1) writes the channel-request and channel-response pair labelled switch, carrying no model, effort or session id.
A switch writes a claude-child process-exit for the old child and a claude-child process-start for the respawned one, under the existing pty.spawn span. viola writes no terminal byte at a respawn.
The switch refusal words dialog-pending, no-session, child-not-ended and resume-failed are channel refusal details only. No diag line emits them, so the diag-line schema does not carry them.

A switch appends one launch line to the events log after the old child is reaped and before the respawn, plus the window line again where the snapshot holds one. The append has no trace of its own (PROVISIONAL).
viola switch has no exit-1 refusal detail of its own. Its exit 1 is the cli catch site's internal-error.

After a respawn the wrapper screens one late session-end of the switched id while the new child lives. Whether a real CLI fires SessionEnd on SIGHUP is unproven (R6a, carried to the fleet on the founder's host).
A send is refused turn-running while a switch stands, from the switch's request until the new child's session-start (PROVISIONAL, F3).

The session added a new CLI verb, viola switch, and a new wrapper channel method, switch, that move a running session to a given model and effort.
On a switch the wrapper ends its own claude child (only the child its own PTY handle holds, no pid lookup), waits up to a new 10 s reap bound, then respawns claude --resume with the recorded session id and the new pair under a new pseudo-terminal behind the same host terminal.
The new pair is recorded in the wrapper's snapshot and as one launch line per switch in the event log so a revive replays it; nothing is written to the user's own Claude settings and no --settings flag is passed.
A switch is refused while the human types, mid-turn, with a dialog pending, on an unverified CLI, with no session or a session id of another shape, when the child does not end within the bound, or when the resume fails; a send is refused turn-running while a switch stands.
The switch is CLI-only (no MCP tool); forks F1, F3, F5 and F6 stand PROVISIONAL on the delegate overseer's word, and the behaviour is proven over the fake agent alone, no capability claimed.

body: A new wrapper channel method, switch, sits beside the contract rows of wrapper channel methods (answer, last, link, pause, release, send, unlink, wait, hook.dialog, hook.event): params v, sender, model?, effort?; reply ok with model and effort, or a refusal; the served requests go from 9 to 10, hook.event still the one notification.

The rule that a new listener or channel method needs a Security Decisions Log entry: switch is a new channel method, served only after the existing peer euid and server checks of the client connect, and is owed its entry (PROVISIONAL, F1).
The decision that CLI frame verbs check the instance first (strict modes first): it does not name switch, which now runs the untrusted-home refusal, then the live endpoint, then the verified connect.
The decision that launch pair flags are checked before anything is read: switch's --model and --effort now go through the same model and effort parsers, and the wrapper re-checks each half.
Wrapper re-validates every input, closed channel types and the -32602 channel error rows: a switch with neither half, a half of another type, or a half failing its check is -32602 with data null.
Self-reported from authenticates nothing and channel from is not an identity: the switch method reads no from at all.

Capability-based all-or-nothing channel access and the same-user trust boundary: any same-user peer that passes the channel checks can now end and restart the session's claude child on another model and effort.

Adopt acts on no process it did not start and the R5 adopt script ends only its own processes: a wrapper now ends its own live child on a switch, killing only the child its own PTY handle holds, with no pid lookup.

Human typing takes the wheel, security refusals never block the human and the human-typing send refusal: switch is refused human-typing while the human types, and refused mid-turn and with a dialog pending (F3, PROVISIONAL).
The unverified CLI gate: switch is refused unverified-cli, read from the start's recorded verification.
viola writes nothing under the Claude home or in Claude's config: the switch keeps the user's settings byte- and mtime-equal and passes no --settings, measured over the fake agent only.

Launch pair kept to the snapshot and the event log, launch pair handed on the child's argv, and the recorded launch pair authenticates nothing: a switch rewrites the snapshot's launch and child_pid, appends one launch line per switch (and the recorded window line again after it), and puts the new pair on the respawned child's argv.
Session id on child argv in a closed shape and as one argv element: the respawn passes the recorded session id to claude --resume; an id of another shape is refused no-session.

Snapshot reference values only after the strict-modes check, replayed snapshot inert, and only the instance's wrapper writes its snapshot: the switch's refusal rungs read the wrapper's own disk snapshot (pending dialog, session id, launch, window), and the wrapper itself rewrites it.
Window record kept to the snapshot and the event log: a switch re-appends the recorded window line after the launch line.

Rules over the claude child's spawn (parent identity variables and inherited CLAUDE credentials stripped, pinned folder first on PATH, run resolves its child program itself, channel handles not inheritable): the respawned child is a new spawn from the wrapper's plan, so each rule now also reaches a respawn.

Rules over the PTY pump and the screen feed (screen feed isolated from passthrough, bounded queue, under a panic catch): the pump now swaps a new pseudo-terminal under the same host stdin and stdout copies, restarts its writer and output threads on the new child, and its panic arm kills the current child.
Bounded time rows: a new compiled time bound, RESPAWN_REAP_BOUND at 10 s (F6, PROVISIONAL); a child not ended within it is not replaced and the switch is refused child-not-ended.

CLI exit-code and instance-unreachable rows (exits 12, 21 and the instance-unreachable causes): viola switch exits 0, 10, 12, 13, 14, 20, 21, with the new refusal words dialog-pending, no-session, child-not-ended and resume-failed at exit 13.

Refusals hold no paths, pids or ids, error messages interpolate nothing and every product error writer named: switch adds a new verb's refusal writer and hints for four new causes; no pair, model or session id appears in any log line.

A child not ended within the bound is not replaced.
While a switch is under way, a send is refused turn-running until the new child's session-start. After that, the old child's late session-end for the switched id is screened once.
Everything was proven over the fake agent alone and no capability is claimed. The forks F1, F3, F5 and F6 are PROVISIONAL on the delegate overseer's word. The live readings R6a and R6b on a real claude are carried to the founder's host. CI on the pre-CI commit was green 7/7.

switch is a CLI-only control verb with no MCP tool (PROVISIONAL, F5).
